ak_godwin_creek.blurb: Godwin Creek is a glacier-fed drainage that feeds 4th of July Creek, which runs into the east side of Resurrection Bay near Seward on the Kenai Peninsula. It is an ice and mixed spot with eight lines, mostly moderate water ice around WI4, one easier flow and one hard WI6 pillar, plus a few mixed lines that reach into the M6 range. The routes sit on the north side of the two-creek drainage, starting just above where the streams join. Some are quick to reach while others are tucked into forested ridges, so expect a bit of route-finding. The setting is coastal and scenic, and it suits parties with solid ice experience.

ak_upper_sky_pilot.blurb: Upper Sky Pilot is a small crag of eight routes on the cliffs above a roadcut along the Seward Highway, south of Eagle River. Climbing is short and slabby, mostly 5.10 with one route at 5.9+, split between sport, trad and top-rope lines. It is the most pleasant of the three crags in the Sky Pilot group, with nice views and a bit of separation from the road. Reaching it takes a short scramble around the left side of the roadcut. There is little here for beginners, but a solid 5.10 climber can fill an afternoon. Wear a helmet, as loose rock is a concern around the other walls nearby.

ak_sea_cliffs_the.blurb: The Sea Cliffs are a small coastal crag on the Juneau road system, regarded as the easier companion to the steeper Hard Sea Cliffs. Eight routes, mostly bolted, run from the 5.5 range through the 5.9s, with a 5.10 and a single 5.12 at the top end. That makes it a sensible choice for newer climbers who want a few easy leads near the water. The cliff catches evening sun, and whales are often spotted from the base. A climbers' trail leads in from a parking spot on the hill before a nearby landmark building.

ak_crackland.blurb: Crackland is a quiet, isolated section on the back of the East Grapefruit dome north of Fairbanks, high above the North Fork of Globe Creek. It faces southeast on a band of limestone and has a handful of short trad and sport lines, plus some that can be top-roped. Grades run from 5.7 up through the 5.10s, with the cracks at the easier end and the sport lines harder. Expect a walk of roughly twenty minutes over talus from the parking lot, and a view out over the valley that makes up for the effort. The routes are still cleaning up, so traffic is light.

ak_19_mile_wall_2.blurb: The 19 Mile Wall is a small cliff above the Richardson Highway in the Valdez area, over a hundred feet tall with a prominent crack running up the middle. It holds a mix of ice lines and trad routes: a few moderate water ice climbs at WI3 and WI4, and trad from 5.7 into the 5.10 range. The wall faces south and is described as a good place to climb in the sun, and it often has workable winter temperatures when town is warmer. Plan for long rappels and bring a couple of ropes or a 70 m rope. Parking beside the road is tight.
